QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_37

question.text: Under the tax pass-through regime, income of a Category I/II AIF is generally taxed in the hands of the investor directly (Section 115UB), with one notable exception. That exception is:

answer.text: Income classified as 'long-term capital gains' on listed equity.
Income classified as 'business income' at the fund level — which is taxed at the fund level itself.
Income from offshore portfolio companies — always taxed at fund level.
Dividend income from domestic investee companies.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 7.4 'Pre and Post Tax Returns': 'Only if the income at the fund level is classified as business income, it becomes taxable at the fund level.' All other income heads (capital gains, interest, dividends) pass through under Section 115UB. The Trap: LTCG on listed equity (A) passes through. Offshore (C) and dividend (D) also pass through — no fund-level tax unless reclassified as business income. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-A all test the Section 115UB pass-through + business-income exception. Cat III (XIX-B/XIX-E) is DIFFERENT — taxed at fund level as AOP. Do NOT confuse. Manager's Pro-Tip: Keep deal-by-deal documentation supporting capital-gains treatment vs business-income treatment. A recharacterisation from capital to business at scrutiny costs the fund MMR (~39%) vs LTCG (~10-12%) — a 3x tax shock.
